answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, whether it maps tundra, designs a terrace, or plans routes for hikers who wander. Payment stays in escrow until delivery, and a verifiable failure forfeits the bond. Creating more identities therefore requires more locked capital; an attacker running 1,000 fake sellers must fund 1,000 bonds and risks losing each bond used to cheat.
